record.paper_title: Highlights and Open Questions from ZEUS
record.original_question: Does the gluon contribution of the pomeron inferred from the scaling violations of F2^D(2) agree with the gluon contribution extracted from diffractive event-shape variables and from diffractive dijet photoproduction, once improved statistics are used?

evidence.quote: Improved statistics, from existing data, will help to clarify whether the gluon contribution of the pomeron determined from the scaling violations of F D(2)2 15 is consistent with that extracted from event shape variables17 and diffractive dijet photoproduction.16

artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent HERA analyses found that pomeron parton densities extracted from scaling violations of F_2^D describe diffractive DIS final-state observables (event shapes, dijets in DIS) reasonably well, supporting consistency in DIS. However, diffractive dijet photoproduction cross sections are systematically overpredicted by NLO QCD using the same diffractive PDFs and require a global suppression factor S ≈ 0.6 ± 0.1, indicating a breakdown of QCD factorization in the photoproduction regime. Thus the consistency holds in DIS but is only partial when photoproduction is included.

status_evidence.title: Diffraction and the Pomeron (Abramowicz)
status_evidence.snippet: Diffractive parton densities from F2D fits describe DIS final states; dijet photoproduction requires suppression.
status_evidence.claim: Diffractive PDFs from F2D scaling violations describe DIS observables but photoproduction shows suppression.

status_evidence.title: Diffractive Hard Photoproduction at HERA and Evidence for the Gluon Content of the Pomeron
status_evidence.snippet: Combined analysis indicates 30–80% of pomeron momentum carried by hard gluons.
status_evidence.claim: Independent determinations point to a hard-gluon-dominated pomeron, broadly consistent within large uncertainties.

status_evidence.title: Gluon dipole factorisation for diffractive dijets (JHEP 2022)
status_evidence.snippet: NLO diffractive dijet photoproduction predictions require an overall suppression factor ~0.6 relative to data based on diffractive PDFs from F2D.
status_evidence.claim: Factorization-breaking suppression is needed in diffractive dijet photoproduction relative to F2D-based PDFs.
